none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a differentiable convex objective over a nonempty closed convex set C in a real Hilbert space. On C, f satisfies the quadratic upper model with public L > 0. A minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0 − xstar‖ ≤ R.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: At each feasible query x, the oracle returns the exact gradient ∇f(x), for every call index and seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same feasible-point query returns the exact value f(x) together with its gradient.

oracle.label: linear_minimization
oracle.details: For feasible x, any r ≥ 0, and any direction g, return an exact minimizer of ⟨g,v⟩ over v ∈ C with ‖v − x‖ ≤ r. Value-gradient queries and local linear-minimization queries share one fixed budget of 3(⌈√(10LR²/ε)⌉ + 1) calls.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/KnownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear.lean: spec.admissible, .inr oracle condition; supplied OracleTemplate.SplitBrox.result budget; LongTails/Template.lean: execute.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public information comprises the real Hilbert space, L > 0, R ≥ 0, ε > 0, feasible x0, and the exact optimum value fstar. The objective f and constraint set C are hidden. The set may be unbounded; R bounds distance to one minimizer rather than the diameter of C. Smoothness inequalities are required only for pairs in C. Local linear minimizers must exist for every admissible query; no oracle-error or independence assumption is needed.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a feasible point output ∈ C satisfying f(output) − f(xstar) ≤ ε, where xstar minimizes f on C and f(xstar) = fstar.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed probability measure, after the fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Smooth constrained convex optimization is classical, but exact access to linear minimization over arbitrary local ball intersections, combined with a publicly known optimum value and Hilbert-space geometry, defines a specialized oracle formulation. No repository implementation or proof was inspected; the literature search does not certify novelty.
